title: Minimum Unlocked Indices to Sort Nums
summary: Given an array nums with values 1, 2, or 3 and a binary array locked of the same length, determine the least number of operations to unlock indices for adjacent swaps that sort nums.
statement: Given an array nums with values 1, 2, or 3 and a binary array locked of the same length, determine the least number of operations to unlock indices for adjacent swaps that sort nums. If sorting is impossible, return -1.
constraints: nums and locked have equal length up to 100,000; nums values are 1, 2, or 3 and locked values are binary.
Adjacent positions i and i+1 may swap only when their values differ by one and locked[i] is zero.
Set locked indices to zero at unit cost; return the minimum cost that makes nums sortable, or -1 if impossible.
hints: A three can never cross a one, while every inverted neighboring-value pair must cross every boundary between its endpoints.
Reject any 3-before-1 inversion; otherwise identify the union of boundaries needed by 2-before-1 and 3-before-2 inversions.
Find the first larger value and last smaller value for each adjacent value pair, then count locked boundaries in those intervals.
All required crossings are possible after those boundaries are unlocked, and every counted boundary is necessary for at least one inversion.
editorial: All required crossings are possible after those boundaries are unlocked, and every counted boundary is necessary for at least one inversion.

tests.explanation: The needed 2-before-1 and 3-before-2 swaps already cross unlocked boundaries, so no operation is needed.
Unlocking boundaries two and five permits all required adjacent swaps, costing two.
